Precalculus | Quarter 2 | Unit 3: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions

The Slow Leak

Solving for time with logarithms

Duration
50 minutes
Grade level
Grades 11–12
Topic
Logarithmic Properties
Standards
HSF-LE.A.4, HSF-BF.B.5, HSA-SSE.A.2

Students apply the product, quotient and power properties and the change-of-base formula, and solve exponential and logarithmic equations, including when a leaking tyre will reach a minimum pressure.

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Expand and condense logarithmic expressions using the product, quotient and power properties.
  • Use the change-of-base formula.
  • Solve exponential equations by taking logarithms.
  • Solve logarithmic equations and reject extraneous solutions.

3Essential question

When an unknown is stuck in an exponent, how do you get it out?

5MTB connection

A slow puncture (or tubeless sealant that hasn’t sealed) loses roughly a fixed percentage of pressure per hour. Solving for t tells a rider whether the tyre will last the ride.

The same algebra answers “how long until…” questions for battery capacity, trail growth and cooling.

The mathOn the trail
Exponential equationPressure after t hours
Taking logsBringing t down from the exponent
Change of baseUsing the ln key for any base
Extraneous solutionA negative time or pressure that the model allows but reality doesn’t

7MTB activity

MTB Problem-Based Exercise

Slow Leak Detective

Build an exponential model for a leaking tyre from two readings and use logarithms to predict when it will be too soft.

You’ll need: Calculator with ln; Optional: a tyre gauge and a real bike

The full lesson plan is for teachers

Teachers also get the mathematical foundation with worked examples, a 5-stage teaching plan with timings, step-by-step activity instructions, 4 guided examples with solutions, 9 practice problems, a 4-question exit ticket, a printable worksheet, common misconceptions, differentiation ideas and the complete answer key.
